content.user_title: Plan a Chrome CSS Inspector Extension
content.value_statement: Planning a browser CSS inspector requires decisions about overlay isolation, inspection metrics, and extension architecture. This guide outlines those decisions without supplying executable extension source.
actual_capabilities: Describe a Manifest V3 architecture using a service worker and a Shadow DOM inspector overlay.
Identify inspection targets including colors, font families, font sizes, margins, padding, and dimensions.
Outline a vanilla JavaScript development workflow without a build tool.
Explain Chrome Developer mode and unpacked extension loading for separately obtained source files.
Document proposed clipboard copying, keyboard toggles, and settings persistence.
Identify stated limits involving protected browser pages, canvas, and SVG internals.
limitations: Only SKILL.md is included; scripts, extension source, and templates are absent.
Runtime behavior, clipboard handling, permissions, and Chrome Web Store readiness cannot be verified from this guide.
The described inspector does not support canvas or SVG internals and has limited access to browser-protected pages.
The documented workflow uses vanilla JavaScript and does not cover React or Vue build steps.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the guide
prompt_templates.prompt: Summarize the inspector described in this guide. Separate documented features from files actually included, and explain what is missing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of the package contents.

prompt_templates.title: Define inspection requirements
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a requirements checklist for a CSS inspector covering colors, fonts, spacing, dimensions, clipboard copying, and keyboard toggling. Include the documented limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Feature planning for a developer and designer.

prompt_templates.title: Plan the extension architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Propose a Manifest V3 architecture for the described inspector using vanilla JavaScript and Shadow DOM. Label implementation proposals separately from documented facts.

prompt_templates.title: Design a verification plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a verification plan for a future implementation covering permissions, clipboard actions, settings persistence, overlay isolation, and protected pages. Do not claim tests passed.

output_examples.input: What is actually included, and can I load it into Chrome?
output: The package contains a public Markdown guide.
Extension scripts, source files, and templates are not included.
You need a separate implementation before using Chrome's Load unpacked option.

output_examples.input: Summarize the inspector requirements for our prototype.
output: Use Manifest V3 and a Shadow DOM overlay.
Inspect element colors, font families, font sizes, margins, padding, and dimensions.
Plan clipboard copying, a keyboard toggle, and persistent settings.
Account for protected browser pages and unsupported canvas or SVG internals.
These are documented requirements, not verified implementation results.

best_practices: Confirm that extension source is available before planning installation or packaging.
Treat advertised features as requirements until an implementation and its permissions have been reviewed.
Test any future implementation on ordinary pages, complex layouts, and browser-protected pages.
anti_patterns: Assuming the guide includes a working extension or executable templates.
Claiming Chrome Web Store approval, runtime safety, or successful tests without implementation evidence.
Expecting the documented inspector to inspect canvas internals or bypass browser page restrictions.

faq.question: Does this package include a working Chrome extension?
faq.answer: No. The public guide explicitly states that scripts, extension source, and templates are not included.

faq.question: Which CSS values does the guide describe?
faq.answer: It describes colors, font families, font sizes, margins, padding, and element dimensions.

faq.question: Does the documented architecture need a build tool?
faq.answer: No. It describes vanilla JavaScript, HTML, and CSS without Webpack, Vite, or NPM build steps.

faq.question: Why does the guide recommend Shadow DOM?
faq.answer: Shadow DOM separates the inspector interface from host page styles. The guide does not include an implementation to verify.

faq.question: How would I install a separate implementation?
faq.answer: After obtaining and reviewing source files, open Chrome's extensions page, enable Developer mode, and select the folder with Load unpacked.

faq.question: Can the described tool inspect every page element?
faq.answer: No. The guide excludes canvas and SVG internals and notes limited inspection on browser-protected pages.
